line: We sign. Who's the observer going to be?

replies.speaker: Adolion Narrator
replies.text:
Quill scratches against parchment as the signatures are added to the forms. Ellie gathers the sheets with a satisfied nod, her eyes lingering for a moment on the party before she tucks them away. "The Guild selects the observer to ensure fairness—you won't know until the morning of the quest. We want the judgment impartial."
*She leans in slightly, her professional tone softening.* "But if you're curious... the high-rank parties tend to announce themselves by their bar tabs at the tavern next door. A-Rank adventurers don't exactly keep a low profile when they're spending their coin."
*Beyond the counter, Tobias has shifted his weight, his gaze drifting toward the window that overlooks the tavern. He looks like a man who has seen too many parties head into that room with confidence, only to come back as strangers or not at all.*

replies.speaker: Tobias
replies.text:
"The Guild does not release the observer's identity beforehand to avoid... undue influence." Tobias's voice is steady, though his fingers tighten almost imperceptibly on the edge of the counter. "It would compromise the exam's integrity."
*He clears his throat, adding with a slight stiffness,* "Though I might suggest you introduce yourselves to the patrons at the tavern this evening. Some of them may be more helpful than they first appear."
*Ellie nods in agreement, though she looks like she wants to say more.*

replies.speaker: Fiana
replies.text:
"A-rankers?" *Fiana glances over her shoulder from where she's wiping down the bar, a teasing smile playing on her lips.* "Sugars, we've got plenty of 'em in here tonight. Though whether they'll be helpful or just loud-mouthed about their exploits is another matter."
*She sets down the rag and leans against the polished wood, her eyes scanning the party members with a keen, assessing look.* "Y'know, I've seen a hundred parties walk through that door with fire in their eyes for the C-rank. Most of 'em come back with stories of glory... and some with stories they'd rather forget."
*Her expression softens for a moment, though the playful glint remains.* "If you're plannin' to sit that exam, you might want to check your gear first. I've seen too many brave souls rush into a C-rank posting with gear suited for D-rank work, and that's a mistake you only make once."

line: Anyone here sat the C-rank exam before? Drinks are on me.

replies.speaker: Fiana
replies.text:
"Well now, sugar, you know how to get attention in a crowd!" *Fiana lets out a bright, melodious laugh and immediately starts pouring ale into tankards.* "But you might have just emptied your coin purse faster than a quest reward."
*Several heads turn toward the table. An older warrior with a scarred face raises a hand from across the room, while a pair of battlemages exchange glances and nod toward the party.*

replies.speaker: Adolion Narrator
replies.text:
The scarred warrior stands and makes his way over, his boots heavy on the tavern floor. He's broad-shouldered and graying at the temples, with a leather-wrapped claymore strapped to his back. When he reaches the table, he settles into a chair with a groan of old joints.
"Took my party three tries to pass," he says, his voice like gravel. "First time, we thought our D-rank gear would hold—a mountain troll nearly took my partner's arm clean off." He eyes the party's equipment with a critical look. "Second time, we fell apart when the observer criticized my leadership. Didn't trust each other after that, and the third time we failed because we were too cautious."

replies.speaker: Kaian
replies.text:
*The kitsune bard doesn't wait for an invitation, gliding over with a graceful sway of his hips and the lute tucked under one arm. He settles into a chair at the edge of the party's table with practiced ease, his wide-brimmed hat shadowing those grey-blue eyes.* "Mind if I join the festivities? The song of the night calls for company, and you lot look like the most interesting thing in this tavern."
*He gives a playful wink to the table at large, then glances toward the scarred warrior with an amused smirk.* "Three tries? That's a tragedy in three acts, my friend. Though I suppose a tragedy makes for better songs than a first-time success."
*He plucks a few idle notes on his lute, the sound bright and clear.* "So you've got a week, is it? Smart to seek counsel. Most parties make the mistake of thinking C-rank is just a harder D-rank quest. But the Guild is testing more than your combat skill—they're testing your synergy, your preparation, your nerves." *His tail flicks with interest.* "And perhaps they want to see if you can actually handle yourselves when things go sideways."

replies.speaker: Dalan
replies.text:
*The elf ranger shifts slightly in his seat, his fingers idly tracing the smooth grain of the table. He hasn't said a word yet, and his green-hooded capelet shadows his face as he watches the conversation unfold with quiet intensity.*
*When Jasira Evergreen's silver-haired silhouette catches the light from across the room, her emerald eyes fix on him with unmistakable intent. She rises from her table in a fluid motion, her white-and-gold robes rustling softly as she makes her way toward the party.*
*She stops beside Dalan and leans down, her long pointed ears visible beneath her silver hair. Her voice is low and sharp as she addresses him in the melodic, flowing syllables of the elven tongue.* "You've chosen a path that will likely end in failure or shame, little brother. A human party will never trust an elf, and you will never lead them properly. Return to the forest where you belong."

He was all sharp edges and nervous energy back then—practically tripped over his own feet half the time. I used to tease him mercilessly just to see his ears flush red." *Her blue eyes twinkle with fondness as she glances back at Tobias.* "Eventually we realized we were the only ones who could actually tolerate each other's company after a long shift. He'd complain about the paperwork, I'd complain about the rowdy patrons, and we'd meet here for a drink to wind down."
*She settles back against the bar, her tone dropping to something almost nostalgic.* "Toby's... well, he's the steady ground I need sometimes. And I'm the one who reminds him to actually have fun now and then." *She winks.* "Even if he still gets flustered when I call him 'sweety' in front of the other Guild staff."

replies.speaker: Tobias
replies.text:
*Tobias's ears twitch visibly at Fiana's words, a faint flush creeping up his neck as he adjusts the stacks of parchment on the counter. He doesn't look up immediately, but his movements grow stiffer as he becomes aware of the conversation.*
"I would appreciate it if you did not broadcast our... working relationship to every patron who enters the tavern." *His voice is refined as ever, though there's a tremor of embarrassment beneath the composure. He finally glances toward their table, ocean-blue eyes meeting theirs for a brief second before returning to the ledger.* "We have known each other for fifteen years. Fiana has... provided necessary levity during times of considerable stress."
*He clears his throat and adds with a slight stiffness,* "And she is correct that I prefer quiet after a shift. Now, if you'll excuse me, I have inventory to complete." *His long fingers wrap around a quill, though his grip is tighter than necessary as he returns to his work.*

line: Fiana, what makes a party fail?

replies.speaker: Adolion Narrator
replies.text:
The tavern is still in its evening lull when the question drops, the crackle of the hearth filling the silence that follows. Fiana doesn't answer immediately; she sets down the glass she was polishing and looks at Max with an expression that's uncharacteristically solemn.
"Most fail because they're afraid," Fiana says, her blue eyes steady and without their usual teasing glint. "Afraid to trust their mates when things get ugly, or too afraid to admit they don't have what it takes for the job. They hide their mistakes, pretend their gear isn't breaking, and then—" she makes a small, sharp gesture with her hand "—everything comes crashing down at once."
*She leans her elbows on the polished bar, her voice dropping.* "But there's another way. The ones who fail for the wrong reasons? They're the ones who stop caring. They get comfortable with D-rank gold, start taking shortcuts, and forget that their mates are counting on them. When a C-rank test comes, they're just going through the motions. And the Guild—the Guild can smell that a mile off."

context.text: Fiana, what makes a party fail?

context.name: Adolion Narrator
context.text:
The tavern is still in its evening lull when the question drops, the crackle of the hearth filling the silence that follows. Fiana doesn't answer immediately; she sets down the glass she was polishing and looks at Max with an expression that's uncharacteristically solemn.
"Most fail because they're afraid," Fiana says, her blue eyes steady and without their usual teasing glint. "Afraid to trust their mates when things get ugly, or too afraid to admit they don't have what it takes for the job. They hide their mistakes, pretend their gear isn't breaking, and then—" she makes a small, sharp gesture with her hand "—everything comes crashing down at once."

The party steps through the door to the adjoining tavern, the warmth of the hearth hitting them along with the smell of roasted meats and ale. The morning crowd is smaller than the night-before rush, with only a few early-risers nursing their morning drinks or planning their day's quests.
*Fiana glances up from where she's wiping down the bar, her blue eyes brightening as she catches sight of them.* "Back already, sugars? That was quick. I just put a pot of coffee on if you need something to wake up to." *She gestures toward a vacant corner table near the window, where the morning light pours in and the view overlooks the Market District below.*
*Dalan settles into a chair, his green-hooded capelet rustling as he leans forward with his elbows on the worn wood. His emerald eyes are sharp and alert, the previous night's flush replaced by a quiet intensity as he looks at Max.*

messages.name: Dalan
messages.text:
"Coffee would be good, thank you." *He speaks softly, his gaze flickering briefly toward the window before settling back on the table.* "We should talk about how we're going to handle the exam. If the observer is going to be testing our synergy, we need to be clear about our roles."
*He reaches down and adjusts the strap of his longbow, making sure it's properly seated against his back. His fingers linger on the polished wood for a moment, a small habit when he's thinking through a problem.* "Belle, as scout, you'll be our eyes and ears. I'll watch the rear and pick off targets before they close. But we need to decide what we do when things go wrong—because they always do."

messages.name: Max Nightriver
messages.text: Dalan, I don't care what your tribe thinks. You're family to the Nightriver party.

messages.name: Dalan
messages.text:
*The elf freezes, his fingers still resting on his bow's strap. For a long moment, he doesn't move or speak, his emerald eyes wide and searching Max's face. When he finally speaks, his voice is barely above a whisper, thick with something between disbelief and profound gratitude.*
"Family..." *He breathes the word like he's tasting it for the first time. His gaze drops to the table, and when he looks up again, there's a glimmer of moisture in his eyes that he quickly blinks away.* "I... I've never—no one in my tribe has ever—" *He stops himself, clearing his throat and squaring his shoulders with renewed determination.*
*He meets Max's gaze directly, his expression now one of quiet, unwavering loyalty.* "Then I will be the best ranger the Nightriver party has ever had. I won't let you down."

line: Put us down for the exam.

replies.speaker: Ellie
replies.text:
Ellie's blue eyes widen as she catches the words, her hands already reaching for the promotion forms with a practiced grace. "Right! Of course!" She spreads the papers across the counter, her fingers steady despite the slight tremor of excitement. "Just a few signatures here, please."
She slides the documents forward, inkwell and pen accompanying them. "Your interview will be in a week's time—I'll personally handle it," she adds, a soft warmth in her voice. "And the quest we'll assign will be a proper C-rank challenge. I'll make sure everything's prepared properly." Her gaze lingers for just a moment on each name before she catches herself and blinks, professional once more.

line: Fiana, what makes a party fail?

replies.speaker: Tobias
replies.text:
Tobias's fingers pause mid-reach, his eyes flicking toward the tavern archway as if checking if anyone else is listening. He clears his throat, straightening his vest with a sudden, precise motion.
"That is a question for the tavern, I fear—Fiana would have her own answer." He glances at the quest board, his voice dropping softer. "But the guild has its records. Most parties do not fail from monsters; they fail from the inside. A disagreement over spoils, a lack of trust in the healer, a leader who does not listen." He looks back at Max, his blue eyes distant. "Or they go out for a rank they are not ready for and come back with one less voice."

line: Dalan, Jasira keeps glaring at you. Who is she to you?

replies.speaker: Dalan
replies.text:
Dalan's gaze flickers to Jasira, then away, a faint flush coloring his cheeks. "She is... a Ranger of our tribe," he says softly, choosing his words with care. "A cousin, though the Evergreen lineage is broad."
He glances back at the silver-haired elf, his expression uncertain. "She does not approve of me being here. Of me leaving the forest to wander with humans." His fingers trace the grain of the wooden table. "She thinks I should return and fulfill my duties to the tribe."

replies.speaker: Jasira
replies.text:
Her emerald eyes narrow as she turns from the fire, her posture straightening with a subtle tension that speaks of years of discipline. "Cousin is one word for it," she says, her voice cold and precise as she switches from elvish back to the common tongue. "She is the daughter of Elder Maraxis and Rewana—my parents. She is my sister, not my cousin."
*She slides into the chair beside Dalan with a fluid, practiced grace, her white-and-gold robes catching the lantern light. Her gaze sweeps over the rest of the table, lingering for a moment on the human and beastfolk before settling back on her brother. The disapproval in her expression is palpable, though her features remain stoic.*
"And yes, I do not approve. Our tribe is under threat from the Zegallan slavers and the demon-taint in the Mountains of Shadow, yet my brother plays adventurer in the human city." *Her voice drops an octave, the words measured and heavy with judgment.* "Father sent me here to 'learn the world,' he said. To broaden my horizons." *The corner of her mouth twitches with a bitterness she cannot quite hide.* "Perhaps I should have stayed and fought."

replies.speaker: Adolion Narrator
replies.text:

Fiana sets down a tray of empty mugs with a sharp clatter, her blue eyes flicking between the siblings before she leans over the bar toward a table of adventurers.
Kaian shifts on his seat by the hearth, his orange tail swishing slowly as he adjusts the lute against his chest. He has been waiting for a gap in the conversation to slide into, a easy smile already forming as he sets aside his instrument.

line: Belle, you've had my back since the first goblin den. I trust you to lead the scouting on the exam.

replies.speaker: Belle
replies.text:
*Belle slams her tankard down on the table with a thud that makes the wood groan. A wild grin spreads across her face, brown eyes alight with pride.* "Damn straight you can trust me!" *She flexes an arm, the muscles in her shoulder bunching beneath the leather pauldrons.* "I can smell a monster's piss before the fucker even knows it's there. And if some prick tries to sneak up on our party—" *She pats the massive stone head of Cleaver where it leans against the table.* "—I'll split 'em wide open before they can blink."
*She leans back in her chair, the wood creaking under her weight, and crosses her arms over her chest. The blade scar under her breast shifts with the movement, though she doesn't seem to notice or care.* "Scouting's easy. The hard part's not getting carried away when I find something worth hitting. But for the exam? I'll keep it tidy. You just make sure we're actually going somewhere with a decent fight, and not just counting sheep in some fuckin' meadow."

replies.speaker: Adolion Narrator
replies.text:
The tavern crowd laughs at Belle's outburst, and a few adventurers at nearby tables raise their mugs in approval. Fiana smiles and shakes her head, already moving to refill Belle's tankard.
"Easy there, big girl," *Fiana says with a wink.* "We don't need you breaking another table. The Guildmaster just finished paying for the last one."

replies.speaker: Fiana
replies.text:
"I'm serious though, sugar," *Fiana leans in over the table, her voice dropping low enough that only the party can hear, her usual flirty tone replaced by something more earnest.* "You're taking your C-rank exam in a week. I've seen too many good folk fail 'cause they went in with F-rank gear and D-rank planning. You want that promotion? Get yourself some proper equipment first."
*She straightens up, her hands on her hips as she scans the party, her blue eyes lingering on their current kit with a critical eye.* "Tavern's got all the gossip—everyone knows the observer parties for C-rank are usually A-rank veterans who don't have patience for amateurs."

line: Tobias, you've always been straight with us. Who might the observer be?

replies.speaker: Tobias
replies.text:
Tobias's hand freezes halfway to his teacup, the porcelain clinking softly against the saucer as his ocean-blue eyes shift toward Max. He looks away quickly, his pale cheeks coloring faintly beneath his short green bangs.
"That is... highly irregular to ask," *he says, his refined voice carrying a hint of his usual stoicism despite the tell-tale flush at his pointed ears.* "Guildmaster Vallie keeps the roster of observers confidential to prevent... undue influence." *He pauses, his long fingers wrapping around the cup with a careful precision that betrays his internal conflict.* "However," *he adds in a softer tone, barely above a whisper,* "I have seen the schedules. If I were a betting elf—which I am not—I would expect someone from 'Will of Steel.' Domas himself might even oversee it, though that would be unusual for a Vice Guildmaster."
*He takes a sip of his tea, the steam curling around his nose.* "But do not trust me over the official process. When Ellie conducts your interview in a week, she will provide you with the necessary details. The observer is there to judge your performance, not to be a secret you need to pry from a receptionist's lips."

Tobias blinks, his flush receding as he refocuses. The sudden shift back to business seems to ground him, though his ears remain slightly pink. "Very well," he says, voice steadying as he pulls the parchment closer. "The terms are straightforward, though not without risk."
*He dips his quill and begins writing their names in elegant script, his movements precise and practiced.* "A week of preparation from this moment. Then a C-rank posting of the Guild's choosing, overseen by an observer. Pass, and you advance. Fail, and you remain at D-rank until next season." *He glances up, blue eyes meeting Max's with a flicker of concern.* "It is a significant step. I hope you have discussed this among yourselves thoroughly."
*He slides the completed form across the counter, ink still wet, and gestures to the empty space beside it.* "I will need each of your signatures here."

context.name: Max Nightriver
context.text: We sign the forms. Ellie, thank you for vouching for us.

context.name: Ellie
context.text:
Ellie's head snaps up, her blue eyes widening in surprise. A rosy blush spreads across her cheeks as she realizes he noticed. "I—that's..." She fidgets with the collar of her dress, unable to meet his gaze for a moment. "It's simply my job to recognize potential, really. I've seen how you handle yourself in the field, and..."
*She trails off, her voice growing quieter, almost shy. Her fingers unconsciously smooth the edge of a parchment on her desk.* "You're very welcome. I have faith in your party."
*Behind the counter, Tobias clears his throat and slides the freshly signed forms away into a folder, his expression neutral but his eyes sharp.*

context.name: Max Nightriver
context.text: Let's head to the tavern for advice over ale.

context.name: Tobias
context.text:
Tobias's eyes track Max toward the tavern arch, then drift to the other party members. A ghost of a smile touches his lips, though it vanishes before it can fully form. "An excellent idea. Rydel is working today, and I suspect she has heard rumors about what sorts of C-rank postings have come through recently."
*He gathers the folder of exam forms and taps them twice against the counter.* "I will be right behind you. I believe the preparation week will be easier to navigate if you know what to expect."
*The tavern beyond the arch is already lively, the scent of roasted meat and ale spilling into the main hall. The evening crowd has begun to gather at the long timber tables, and the sound of laughter and clinking tankards drifts through.*

line: Fiana, what makes a party fail?

replies.text:
Fiana slides a tray of tankards onto a nearby table, then turns her attention to Max with a knowing smile. "Honey, you'd be surprised how often it isn't the monsters that do 'em in."
*She leans against the bar, propping one elbow on the polished wood while her blue eyes study the party.* "Most of the ones who fail the C-rank? They show up with D-rank gear and C-rank ambition. One of their blades snaps, their shield gets too dented to hold, or their healer runs out of supplies because they didn't prepare."
*Her expression softens, though there's still a sharp edge to her gaze.* "It's never just the quest itself. It's the small things—the rusty joints in a sword or the leather that's too frayed to last a proper scrap. That's what kills 'em, usually."

line: Morning. We find Domas and ask about the posting.

replies.speaker: Adolion Narrator
replies.text:
The guild hall is quiet at this hour, the morning light slanting through tall windows and illuminating dust motes in the air. The scent of old parchment and floor wax lingers, and the scrape of a broom echoes from somewhere in the back.
Domas is already at his station, hunched over the main desk with a ledger open and a stack of fresh forms beside him. He doesn't look up immediately, his quill scratching methodically across the page as he finishes a line. Then he glances up, his red eyes taking in the party and the way they've clearly been waiting for him.
"Ah. The exam applicants," Domas says, his tone polite but measured. He sets the quill aside with a soft tap and clasps his hands on the desk. "I trust you've had your week of preparation. I was just reviewing the available postings." *He reaches for a separate folder, pulling out three distinct parchments.* "Three options have come across my desk. Two are standard C-rank contracts. One is..." *He pauses, his expression growing more serious.* "...an irregular request."
